question.problem: What is the distance between the points $(-\sqrt{3},2\sqrt{3})$ and $(3\sqrt{3},5\sqrt{3})?$
question.worked_solution:
In this case, we have ${{(-\sqrt{3},2\sqrt{3})}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{1}\text{,}\,{y}_{1})}$ and ${{(3\sqrt{3},5\sqrt{3})}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{2}\text{,}\,{y}_{2})}.$
So, the distance $d$ can be calculated using the distance formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\sqrt{({x}_{2}-{x}_{1})^{2}+({y}_{2}-{y}_{1})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(3\sqrt{3}-(-\sqrt{3}))}^{2}+{(5\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(4\sqrt{3})^{2}+(3\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16(3)+9(3)} \\  & =\sqrt{48+27} \\  & =\sqrt{75} \\  & =5\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
